facts.label: Planejar um passeio
facts.sub: Use how far para a distância e going to para planos: How far is the café? We’re going to stop at the café. We’re not going to be late.

facts.label: How far
facts.sub: Para perguntar a distância, use How far + is/are: How far is the lake? How far is the café? A resposta usa kilometers: Ten kilometers. Five kilometers from here.

facts.label: Going to
facts.sub: Para planos, use am/is/are going to + verbo base: We’re going to stop at the café. I’m going to bring a map. Para negar, use are not going to: We’re not going to be late.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

We say “How far it is?” → Falso (We say How far is it?)

pages.title: A bright park · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a bright Saturday morning in a park in Ottawa. A smooth path goes along the river. Quinn stands next to her red bike. A small bridge crosses the water. Her friend Theo arrives with his helmet. Quinn asks about the ride.
“Hi, Theo! Are you going to ride on the new bike path?” says Quinn. “Yes! How far is it?” says Theo. “It’s ten kilometers from the bridge to the lake.” says Quinn.
